summary: Vector encoding bitflip during proxy recode causing sparse top-k suppression and rerank p95 spike
description:
Issue summary: Customers report intermittent downward shifts in rerank quality and a tail latency (p95) spike starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. The symptom cluster includes missing candidates in top-k for queries that previously returned stable results and a concurrent increase in rerank p95 from ~180ms to ~720ms for affected tenants.
Impact: Multiple enterprise customers (Lexiva Health confirmed) experiencing production search regressions and elevated error/retry rates; business workflows blocked for some pipelines.
Environment: Production, us-east region, requests flow through the API gateway -> envoy proxy -> embedding encode/serialize -> embeddings-service -> reranker.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Submit stable test query set used by customer (lexiva-search-suite v2026-02) against embeddings endpoint via prod API key. 2) Observe embedding payload sizes and base64 header flags on the proxy logs. 3) Call rerank endpoint with the same embedding vectors and compare top-10 sets before/after proxy restart. 4) Observe intermittent missing candidates and score shifts.
Logs / notable traces: - envoy-proxy logs show repeated short-lived warnings about "recode buffer overflow" around 2026-03-09T22:05:12Z. - embeddings-service logged occasional value-clamped warnings: "float->int cast truncated non-zero mantissa". - reranker traces show higher-than-normal KV cache misses and an increase in ANN fallback use. - Customer provided request IDs: r-lexiva-0001, r-lexiva-0007 (attached in customer upload).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 — Priya Singh (Support): Acknowledged receipt from Lexiva, raising as P1. Collected request IDs and asked for reproducer set. SLA first response met.
2026-03-10 10:02 — Marcus Lee (SRE): Noted spikes in p95 and found proxy recode warnings in same window. Routing to proxy team to investigate binary recode path.

2026-03-10 12:45 — Lina Martinez (Proxy Eng): Hypothesis: a recent optimization to compress embedding payloads introduced a scalar recode that coerces float32->int16 for micro-batches under 1KB. Running canary with compression disabled.
2026-03-10 16:30 — Lexiva Health (Customer): Confirmed that disabling compression on their side reduced missing-topk frequency in the short test run. Asked for ETA on full fix.

2026-03-11 08:10 — Marcus Lee (SRE): Deployed proxy hotfix to stablize recode path in us-east canary (proxy-1849). Monitoring metrics and comparing rerank topk drift. Early metrics show reduction of missing candidates and p95 returning toward baseline.
2026-03-12 11:05 — Priya Singh (Support): Notified Lexiva of rollback and mitigation; scheduling postmortem and follow-up tests with customer QA team.
2026-03-12 11:20 — Lexiva Health (Customer): Thanks — will run extended regression overnight and report if anything persists.
investigation_notes: Initial correlation: p95 spike aligns with repeated proxy recode warnings. No upstream deployment at embeddings-service or reranker in that window.

Observed that compressed payload path applies a cast intended for a legacy codec. Under edge-case micro-batch sizes, codec dropped mantissa bits leading to near-duplicate vectors after normalization (aliasing).

Aliasing leads to candidate de-duplication heuristics in reranker to prune duplicates, which in turn suppressed legitimate near-duplicate top-k hits causing quality drop. The numeric change also increased ANN fallback due to distance thresholds being affected, raising p95.
Reproducer: running lexiva-search-suite with deterministic seeds reproduced the issue in ~1/20 runs; more frequent on queries with many short tokens and emojis (UTF-8 multi-byte).
Telemetry: added temporary histogram on "embed-mantissa-entropy" and a counter for "recode-truncation" to catch further occurrences; ingestion pipeline now emits these metrics.
Related: linked archived incident SUP-331210 shows a previous embedding-rotation bug but not identical; kept as reference.
Risk assessment: Fix touches the proxy recode path which is critical; need staged rollout and regression tests for small-batch/emoji-heavy payloads.
resolution: Hotfix applied: proxy PR #1849 disables legacy scalar recode for payloads flagged as float32; proxy canary deployed to us-east and verified for 24h with Lexiva test suite.
Rollback: temporarily disabled compression optimization in envoy config to remove the recode step while permanent patch is validated.
Data remediation: reprocessed 3 hours of affected embedding writes for Lexiva to recover suppressed candidates where backlog processing allowed (customer-approved).

Post-incident actions: 1) Add unit/integration tests covering float32 preservation for micro-batches and UTF-8 emoji payloads. 2) Add checksum/version header validation on embedding payloads and reject/alert on unexpected recode. 3) Schedule follow-up changelist to reintroduce safe compression behavior with explicit type checks (owner: Lina Martinez).
Customer communication: Sent interim postmortem and action items; plan a joint validation window before closing the ticket.
Next steps: Close after 72-hour clean window and customer sign-off; create a related internal task INT-12045 for long-term compression strategy.
